neighbours.label: Pressure-driven flow: a force pushing a fluid or electric current through a conduit (blood through vessels, water through pipes, current through a circuit)
fire: A booster pump raises the pressure so water can flow uphill to the storage tank.
As blood flows into the capillaries, the arterial pressure drops sharply.
When a voltage is applied across the wire, current flows through it.
The sump pump pushes groundwater out through a discharge pipe.
With each contraction the heart drives blood into the aorta.
The fire hose needs enough pressure to send water to the top floor.
Hydraulic fluid is forced through the lines to move the piston.
Root pressure pushes sap up through the trunk to the leaves.
quiet: The blood on the floor had dried to a dark brown stain.
Her blood type is O negative, which the clinic always needs.
The water in the glass had gone warm by the afternoon.
He felt under pressure to finish the report before Friday.
Current events are discussed in the first hour of the class.
The electricity bill was higher than usual in January.
A hose lay coiled on the lawn next to the shed.
The pump at the gas station was out of order all weekend.

predictions: Flow-through items reach 0.35-0.9; blood, water, pressure, current and pump used without a driven flow (blood type, warm water in a glass, under pressure to finish, current events, pump out of order) stay under 0.15.
short: pressure pushing flow through a conduit
notes: Probe: voltage drives current through a circuit 0.906, blood pressure / pump blood through the body 0.710, heart pumps more blood 0.480, pressure pushes water through pipes 0.361; blood test 0.095, reservoir gates 0.109, cabin air pressure 0.062, peer pressure 0.008, museum hours 0.029. The + pole's logit effect suppresses ' pressure', ' flow', ' pump', ' drop', so this pole promotes pressure-and-flow vocabulary: a predictor of the hydraulic frame rather than a response to one word.
